title: What training does the NRC require for nuclear power plant personnel?
description: NRC training rules for nuclear power plants: the 10 CFR 50.120 systems approach to training and 10 CFR 55.59 licensed operator requalification explained.
shortAnswer: The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) requires each nuclear power plant licensee to run a training program derived from a systems approach to training under 10 CFR 50.120, covering nine categories of non-licensed and support personnel. Licensed reactor operators and senior operators must also complete a requalification program under 10 CFR 55.59 lasting no more than 24 months, pass a comprehensive written examination, and pass an operating test every year.
keyTakeaways: Section 50.120 applies to holders of and applicants for operating licenses under Part 50 and holders of combined licenses under Part 52, with the program in place 18 months before fuel load.

A systems approach to training is defined in 10 CFR 55.4 by five elements: job analysis, learning objectives, design and implementation from the objectives, evaluation of trainee mastery, and evaluation and revision based on job performance.
Licensed operators must complete a requalification program run as a continuous cycle of no more than two years, a comprehensive written examination, and an annual operating test under section 55.59.
To keep an active license, an operator must perform licensed functions on at least seven 8 hour or five 12 hour shifts per calendar quarter under section 55.53(e).
Operator licenses expire after six years under section 55.55, and renewal under section 55.57 requires a facility statement that the requalification program was completed.
appliesTo: Holders of and applicants for nuclear power plant operating licenses under 10 CFR Part 50
Holders of combined licenses under 10 CFR Part 52

Non-licensed operators, shift supervisors, shift technical advisors, instrument and control technicians, electrical and mechanical maintenance personnel, radiological protection and chemistry technicians, and engineering support personnel
Individuals holding NRC reactor operator and senior reactor operator licenses under 10 CFR Part 55

sections.heading: Which NRC rules govern training at a nuclear power plant?

blocks.text: Two rules carry most of the weight. [10 CFR 50.120](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/10/50.120) requires the plant licensee to run a training and qualification program for nine named categories of personnel, and [10 CFR Part 55](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/chapter-I/part-55/subpart-F/section-55.59) governs the individuals who hold reactor operator and senior reactor operator licenses, including their requalification.

The two layers have different subjects. Section 50.120 places duties on the facility licensee for its workforce. Part 55 licenses individuals, and section 55.53 makes completion of the requalification program in section 55.59 a condition of every operator license, whether or not it is stated on the license.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects 10 CFR 50.120 and 10 CFR Part 55 as published in the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations as at November 2026. Section 55.59 was most recently amended at 89 FR 106253 (December 30, 2024).

sections.heading: What does 10 CFR 50.120 require of the training program?

blocks.text: Section 50.120 requires a training program derived from a systems approach to training that provides for the training and qualification of nine categories of personnel. Operating license applicants must establish it by 18 months before fuel load, and combined license holders must have it in place, as described in the final safety analysis report, no later than 18 months before the scheduled initial fuel load.

The nine categories in section 50.120(b)(2) are: non-licensed operator, shift supervisor, shift technical advisor, instrument and control technician, electrical maintenance personnel, mechanical maintenance personnel, radiological protection technician, chemistry technician, and engineering support personnel.

Paragraph (b)(3) adds four ongoing duties. The program must provide qualified personnel to operate and maintain the facility safely in all modes of operation, comply with the facility license including technical specifications, be periodically evaluated and revised to reflect industry experience and changes to the facility, procedures, regulations and quality assurance requirements, and be periodically reviewed by licensee management for effectiveness. Sufficient records must be kept available for NRC inspection to verify the adequacy of the program.

sections.heading: What is a systems approach to training in NRC terms?

blocks.text: The NRC defines a systems approach to training in [10 CFR 55.4](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/chapter-I/part-55/subpart-A/section-55.4) as a training program that includes five elements. It is the same idea as the [ADDIE model](/glossary/addie-model), written as a regulatory definition.

items: Systematic analysis of the jobs to be performed.
Learning objectives derived from the analysis which describe desired performance after training.
Training design and implementation based on the learning objectives.
Evaluation of trainee mastery of the objectives during training.
Evaluation and revision of the training based on the performance of trained personnel in the job setting.

blocks.text: The fifth element is the one most often weak in practice, because it requires evidence from the job setting rather than from the classroom. A licensee that can trace a learning objective back to a task in its [job task analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-job-task-analysis) and forward to a field performance indicator has the chain the definition describes.

sections.heading: What does licensed operator requalification under 10 CFR 55.59 involve?

blocks.text: Each licensed operator and senior operator must complete a Commission approved requalification program conducted for a continuous period not exceeding 24 months, pass a comprehensive requalification written examination, and pass an annual operating test. When one cycle ends, the next must follow promptly on a continuous schedule.

Section 55.59(c) sets the content of a program that is not built on a systems approach to training. It requires preplanned lectures on nine subjects, including theory and principles of operation, plant protection systems, engineered safety systems, normal, abnormal and emergency operating procedures, radiation control and safety, and technical specifications. It also requires on the job training in control manipulations, review of all abnormal and emergency procedures on a regularly scheduled basis, and awareness of facility design, procedure and license changes.

The control manipulations in paragraph (c)(3)(i)(A) to (L) must be performed annually, including plant or reactor startups, plant shutdown, loss of coolant, loss of electrical power, loss of feedwater and loss of service water where required for safety. The remaining manipulations, items (M) to (AA), are performed on a two year cycle, and manipulations not performed at the plant may be performed on a simulator. In lieu of the prescriptive lecture, on the job training and evaluation content, the Commission may approve a program developed using a systems approach to training.

Evaluation under paragraph (c)(4) includes written examinations and annual operating tests that identify retraining needs, systematic observation of performance by supervisors or training staff, simulation of emergency or abnormal conditions, and an accelerated requalification program for any operator whose evaluations clearly show the need.

sections.heading: How do operators keep a license active and renew it?

blocks.text: Under [10 CFR 55.53(e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-10/chapter-I/part-55/subpart-F/section-55.53), a licensee at a power reactor must actively perform operator or senior operator functions on at least seven 8 hour or five 12 hour shifts per calendar quarter. An operator who falls short may not resume licensed duties until the facility certifies that their qualifications are current and that they have completed at least 40 hours of shift functions under direction, including a complete plant tour and all required shift turnover procedures.

Operator and senior operator licenses expire six years after issuance under section 55.55, or earlier on termination of employment with the facility licensee. Renewal under section 55.57 is filed on Form NRC-398 and requires a statement from the facility licensee that the applicant satisfactorily completed the requalification program during the license term, together with evidence of competent and safe performance. Filing at least 30 days before expiry keeps the existing license in force until the NRC decides.
Section 55.53 also requires a biennial medical examination and participation in the fitness for duty drug and alcohol testing programs under 10 CFR Part 26 for licensees at power reactors.

sections.heading: What training records must be kept?

blocks.text: Section 55.59(c)(5) requires the facility licensee to keep records documenting each licensed operator's participation in requalification, including copies of written examinations, the answers given, the results of evaluations, documentation of operating tests, and any additional training given in areas of deficiency. These records are retained until the operator's license is renewed.

For the wider workforce, section 50.120(b)(3) requires sufficient records to maintain program integrity, available for NRC inspection. The rule does not set a fixed retention period for those records, so the period belongs in the plant's records program. The guides on [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records) and [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) cover how to structure them, and the broader picture for [energy and resources organizations](/industries/energy-resources) is on the industry page.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents the job analysis, learning objectives and assessment points as linked framework elements, so the trace from task to objective to evaluation that a systems approach to training depends on is explicit. When a procedure or design change lands, the affected objectives and personnel categories can be identified for the periodic revision that section 50.120 requires.

faqs.q: Does 10 CFR 50.120 cover licensed reactor operators?
faqs.a: Section 50.120 lists nine categories, including shift supervisors and non-licensed operators, but licensed reactor operators and senior operators are governed by 10 CFR Part 55, which sets license conditions, examinations and the requalification program in section 55.59. Section 55.59(c) lets the Commission approve a requalification program developed using a systems approach to training, so both programs can share one analysis base.

faqs.q: Can the NRC administer requalification exams itself?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 55.59(a)(2)(iii) allows the Commission, in lieu of accepting the facility licensee's certification that an operator passed exams within an approved systems approach program, to administer a comprehensive requalification written examination and an annual operating test directly.

faqs.q: What happens if an operator fails requalification?
faqs.a: Under section 55.59(b), if the requalification requirements are not met, the Commission may require the licensee to complete additional training and submit evidence of successful completion before returning to licensed duties. The program must also provide for accelerated requalification where evaluations clearly show the need.

faqs.q: Do non-power reactors have the same requalification rules?
faqs.a: Not identically. Section 55.59(c)(7) allows requalification programs at utilization facilities licensed under Part 50 that are not power reactors to conform generally to, but not be identical to, the power reactor program. Active status for non-power reactor licensees is a minimum of four hours per calendar quarter under section 55.53(e).

factCheck.claim: Section 50.120 applies to operating license applicants and holders and combined license holders; program established 18 months before fuel load; derived from a systems approach to training; nine named personnel categories
Section 50.120(b)(3) requires periodic evaluation and revision, periodic management review for effectiveness, and sufficient records available for NRC inspection
Section 55.4 defines a systems approach to training by five elements

Section 55.59 requires a requalification program not exceeding 24 months, a comprehensive written examination and an annual operating test; control manipulations (A) to (L) annually and others on a two year cycle; records kept until license renewal

Section 55.53(e) requires seven 8 hour or five 12 hour shifts per calendar quarter for active status, four hours for non-power reactors; 55.53(f) requires 40 hours of shift functions under direction to reactivate; 55.53(i) biennial medical examination
Operator licenses expire six years after issuance; renewal application filed 30 days before expiry keeps the license in force
Renewal requires a facility statement that the applicant satisfactorily completed the requalification program during the license term, filed on Form NRC-398
Section 55.59 last amended at 89 FR 106253, December 30, 2024
